newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast prods rise with NYMEX, shut diesel unit.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast prods rise with NYMEX, shut diesel unit.

text.p: U.S. West Coast products prices ended higher Wednesday, brokers said, following the shutdown Monday of a diesel-making unit at ARCO's Los Angeles-area refinery.
Workers shut the 4,000 barrel-per-day hydrocracker to repair a leak that caused production of off-spec diesel fuel.

ARCO officials said they bought 60,000 barrels of diesel to cover the unit's lost output, sending up terminal prices eight cents since Monday and boosting pipeline offers five cents to 85 cents a gallon.
"They're trying to slow down their rack sales. The have to buy to cover their (shutdown)," a broker said.
Meanwhile, prices for NYMEX heating oil rose just over two cents a gallon to 68.84 cents, with gasoline up 1.19 cents to 68.23 cents. Short covering of heating oil spurred the rally, traders said.
Offers for California CARB diesel rose one cent from Tuesday to 85 cents a gallon, while sellers of low sulphur grade asked for 74 cents a gallon, or 0.50 cents more than yesterday, traders said.
In gasoline markets, San Francisco conventional gasoline was sold at 76 Wednesday, unchanged from Tuesday prices, traders said.
Los Angeles conventional gasoline was the same price as the Bay grade, while CARB in L.A. rose a penny to 81/82 cents.
